script: Could Brighton actually win the Premier League this season? Brighton are third in the Premier League with 13 points after six games, only two behind Man City and Arsenal, and they've scored 18 goals while conceding just five. They beat defending champions Arsenal 3-0 at home. And after that result, 14 out of 17 bookmakers slashed their odds to finish top six, which is insane to think about since The Guardian predicted them to finish ninth this year. While they have the youngest manager in the league in Fabian Hürzeler, who just locked in a contract extension through 2029. But even after a big win against Arsenal and an international break, they didn't slow down. Brighton went to Sunderland with only 38% possession and took the lead in the 53rd minute, then got a red card 4 minutes later. They were down to 10 men for over half an hour and still scored again in stoppage time to win 2-0. Title winners grind out results like that, and Leicester won the whole thing in 2015/16 at 5,000-to-one odds. So we know it's possible. But here's where things could come back to reality. Brighton's next three Premier League games are Crystal Palace, Liverpool away, then Man City away, and they're also playing in the Conference League this season, which means midweek European games with a squad that lost some key players over the summer window. On top of that, Hürzeler has managed 11 Premier League games in December and has never won a single one. So realistically, they're probably not winning the title, but a top four finish is genuinely on, and those next three weeks will tell us everything.
